title: The Sanctum of Saturnia
dek: Scribonia leads a company beneath Mage’s Ruin in search of Saturnia’s surviving work. Oya’s quick thinking saves them from the first gauntlet; deeper inside, the difference between finding history and carrying it away becomes fatal.

facts.Setting: Mage’s Ruin, high in Gael’s mountains
facts.People: Scribonia; Minerva; Oya; Lady Severina; Ruben
facts.Outcome: Four escape the collapsing sanctum. Minerva dies in the waters below; the gathered relics are not brought out.
facts.Discovery: A warded sanctuary associated with Saturnia; Scribonia leaves with information, not the central book.

body:
Scribonia comes to Mage’s Ruin seeking the work of the figure he calls his mother. He has never met Saturnia; later in the descent he explains that the kinship is spiritual and any direct ancestry uncertain. The search is personal enough to draw him into danger, but five people will have to live with its decisions. Minerva arrives eager for an untouched history. Oya is nervous. Ruben has come to help, and Severina promises to do what she can to keep them safe.

A cover made to hide what lies below

The entrance is concealed beneath lead. Ruben studies it and recognizes a hastily laid covering rather than a wall built to withstand an assault. Scribonia reads its purpose as concealment from magical inspection. Minerva’s blasts, Oya’s staff and kicks, and Øblivion’s weight gradually force a way through.

Dust rises around them. Ruben covers his face and repeatedly warns the company; Oya later suffers from the exposure and uses restoration on herself. The tunnel beyond is lit by long-burning arcane braziers. It has waited far longer than their argument over how to enter.

The first visible wards stop the advance. Minerva finds what looks like a path between them, but Scribonia warns that touch need not be their trigger. Rather than spend his power undoing every visible defence, he teleports the company farther down the corridor.

The one person still able to move

They arrive on another danger. Dust conceals symbols beneath Oya and Severina. Scribonia asks them to hold still, then lets them step away while he examines the markings. The movement releases a concussive blast. Everyone but Oya is caught helpless as the corridor begins working through its defences.

Harpoons strike first, followed by falling stone, explosions and seeking missiles. Oya tries to shake Scribonia free, then tries dragging him into a crevice. She cannot shift him quickly enough. The answer comes from the wind she had offered to use outside: she redirects it to move her companions toward shelter.

She keeps adjusting that barrier as the assault changes, heals Ruben and gets the company into the wall before the remaining traps sweep past. An antimagic burst drains much of their equipment’s stored power. Poison darts, a false dragon and a rolling boulder pass the refuge they have reached. Oya breaks down once they are safe; the others thank her. The healer who feared the expedition has just kept it alive.

A voice in Saturnia’s name warns them to turn back. Scribonia suspects a recorded magical warning, not a conversation with the living goddess. He wants to continue. Ruben, bloodied and uncertain he can withstand another such passage, demands more care. Minerva initially defends the archmage’s judgment.

What caution has to change

Scouting ahead through his spectral companion, Scribonia locates a door in the ceiling and another stretch of passage. He opens a portal toward it. An ordinary mechanical trap snaps shut on Oya’s leg. Magical sight has not made the physical defences harmless.

Scribonia pulls her free by teleportation. Healing alone will not restore the shattered limb, so he weaves stronger restorative magic around it like silk. The bone and tissue mend. Oya tests the leg and hugs him, relieved. Minerva is now less certain that Ruben’s objections were misplaced.

For the final approach, Scribonia goes through first and checks the landing before calling the others. The company reaches the ceiling door. Its unfinished sequence is tied to life magic. Oya’s first attempt makes the structure shake; after discussion, Scribonia supplies the paired signs that open it.

They climb into a dark sanctuary heavy with magic. Ruben helps with rope and his broom. Beyond another great door, Scribonia finds a boundary where his own magic ceases to work. The search has brought him closer to Saturnia’s work while stripping away the power on which he usually relies.

The book and the things left beside it

Minerva digs a tablet from the rubble and finds teleportation sigils on it. She continues searching. Ruben uncovers a staff and a wand; Severina finds an amulet. The finds draw different responses. Scribonia hesitates over a glowing sphere held by a skeleton, conscious that he is entering someone else’s sanctuary. Minerva wraps the sphere and takes it, intent on preserving what the ruin contains.

Severina and Oya open the heavy door together. Inside stands a device with four spheres and a book at its center. Scribonia feels the book calling to him. He remembers an earlier occasion when that feeling of worthiness led him badly astray, and stops long enough to question it.

He opens it. The reading absorbs him while his companions continue looking among broken stairs and arcane conduits. Then the doors slam. A voice condemns the intruders for taking what is not theirs, and the ceiling begins to crack.

Ruben and Oya try to rouse Scribonia. Shaking him does not pull him from the text. Falling stone finally does. The book burns to ash. Whatever he has learned, he will not carry that volume out of the chamber.

What they have to leave behind

Moth wings appear on the company as daylight breaks through the failing roof. Flight offers an escape, but anyone trying to take the gathered objects finds them impossibly heavy. Magic cannot simply lift the burden away.

Severina drops the amulet. Ruben relinquishes what he has collected. Freed of the objects, they can rise. Severina stays close to the badly hurt Ruben and gets him to Øblivion outside. Oya escapes too. Scribonia remains near those still below rather than immediately leaving them.

Minerva will not discard her bag. To her, the objects are history worth saving, not merely treasure. The others plead with her. Oya argues that no find is worth her life; Scribonia tells her that things which have lain buried for ages can remain buried. A side passage is already blocked and the doors have shut.

She chooses the waterfall at the back of the sanctum, hoping for a way through the water below. Scribonia dives after her and catches her, but trying to lift her feels like raising a mountain. She asks him to let her fall.

The water does not carry her home

There is one final offer: Scribonia can burn away his own spellbook, Saturnia, to lift Minerva. The ruling explicitly concerns the spellbook, not the goddess herself, his knowledge of her or their connection. Scribonia declines. Even after that distinction is clarified, he lets Minerva go, believing her insistence that she may survive. He promises to find her.

The current takes her into darkness. A falling boulder strikes her before she leaves the area where magic fails. Unconscious and helpless beneath the water, she cannot use the escape she imagined. The narrator confirms her death. Her hope of reaching another cavern, and Ruben’s later dreams of other possible endings, do not become a return.

Scribonia flies out last and watches the sanctuary collapse. Four members of the company have escaped. The objects gathered inside have not. He says he has gained information worth more than the things they could not take, but the contents of that discovery are not supplied here.

The news reaches Eovar through Ruben. Nerias remembers a champion and leader; Bohlale breaks the glass in his hand in shock. Ruben gives a much harsher judgment of Minerva. Their disagreement belongs to the aftermath. The quest establishes how she died without requiring everyone who knew her to agree on the life that preceded it.

People and connected histories Minerva · Scribonia · Oya · Severina · Saturnia · Alpine Forest · Library of Nuru
